headline: GrapheneOS ported to Android 17 with official releases coming soon
summary: The privacy-focused mobile OS has been successfully ported to the latest Android version, with initial releases expected imminently.
details: GrapheneOS, a privacy and security-focused mobile operating system, has officially announced its port to Android 17. The team has been working diligently to adapt the OS to the latest Android version, ensuring continued security and privacy for its users.

The development team has confirmed that the GrapheneOS code for Android 17 is being pushed to public repositories. They are currently building a final official release based on Android 16 QPR2, with the initial Android 17 release scheduled for tomorrow.

Testing of the Android 17 port has already been successfully conducted on a range of Pixel devices, including the Pixel 6a, 7, 7a, 8, 10a, 10, and 10 Pro Fold. This extensive testing ensures compatibility and stability across supported hardware.

Users will soon be able to build and test the Android 17 version of GrapheneOS themselves, as the code becomes fully accessible. Public testing for official releases is slated to commence tomorrow, allowing the community to contribute to the final polish.
